clue.text: Description of northern region round pagan rim

indicators.note: round suggests the letters being turned about and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A pagan site's rim is mentioned in an account of a northern area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the anagram signal on PAGAN RIM. GRAMPIAN was the name of a Scottish local-government region around Aberdeen, and the word also describes things belonging to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Grampian is the adjective and name for the former region of north-east Scotland, so it describes that northern area.

clue.text: Has her man been turfed out?

definitions.text: Has her man been turfed out?

parts.words: Has her man been turfed out?
parts.note: reads as a wife whose husband has been thrown out of the house, or even buried under the turf; really a woman whose husband is often away

explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose husband is temporarily absent, idiomatically pictured as left alone while he is off elsewhere.

clue.text: Emphasise account with money at EU possibly

parts.note: a cent is a small unit of money

indicators.note: possibly says the letters given could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A bank stresses an account holding cash at the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: To accentuate something is to stress or highlight it, a direct synonym of emphasise.

clue.text: High-flyer has a seat on it

parts.note: a pew is a seat in church
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird perches on its own seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The pewit or peewit is the lapwing, a bird, so literally something that flies high.

clue.text: Porter's air indicating complete toleration?

definitions.meaning: a song (air) by Cole Porter, the American songwriter
the phrase means every kind of behaviour is permitted

explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter wrote the musical and song of this title; the phrase itself means nothing is forbidden.

clue.text: Sleeveless garment worn in army with dull back

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: back tells us the word for dull is read in reverse order

parts.note: drab means dull or colourless

explanation.surface: A plain sleeveless coat is worn by soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force, a staple crossword source of two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a short sleeveless tunic, as worn by heralds, so it is a garment without sleeves.

clue.text: Understanding of a conflict involved sense

parts.note: a war is a conflict

indicators.note: involved, meaning tangled or complicated, signals the letters of sense are mixed up

explanation.surface: Grasping a war requires an intricate feel for things.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness is knowledge or perception of a situation, a close synonym of understanding.

clue.text: Sharp, but nonetheless a sucker

parts.note: reads as a shrewd person who is still gullible; really a tart sweet that one sucks

explanation.definitionFit: A boiled sweet with a sour taste, so it is both tart in flavour and something sucked.

clue.text: See 7
Cunning methods for constructing vaulted passages

parts.note: arch means slyly cunning or mischievous
ways are methods of doing things

explanation.surface: Crafty techniques are used to build arched corridors.
explanation.definitionFit: Archways are passages beneath arches, so they are vaulted passages.

clue.text: Girl cut into firm material

indicators.note: into says the trimmed name goes inside the abbreviation for firm

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: cut means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl cuts into a sturdy piece of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm material' reads as one phrase about sturdy cloth, but firm belongs to the wordplay and material alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain cotton fabric, so it is a type of material.

clue.text: Sweet yellow stuff to drink

parts.note: butter is a yellow dairy spread
Scotch is whisky, a drink

explanation.surface: A sugary yellow liquid is offered as a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard brittle confection, so it is a kind of sweet.

clue.text: University building programme European Union has seen to

indicators.note: to programme is to arrange or set out, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An EU building scheme has been dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'programme' looks like a noun in the surface but works as the anagram signal on EU, HAS and SEEN TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Senate House is the central administrative building of the University of London, and the name is used at other universities too.

clue.text: Party item to sit out, being in the air

parts.note: a balloon is a decoration at a party

indicators.note: out, as in out of order, says the letters of sit are disarranged

explanation.surface: A party balloon sits out, floating aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is read as a noun: a creature that is up in the air, not a verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: A balloonist flies in a balloon, so is a person aloft in the sky.

clue.text: Black is one in beginnings of the depression, dumped

parts.note: jet is an intensely black colour

indicators.note: in places these two words inside the opening letters that follow
beginnings of picks the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Black is one of the starts of a slump, and was thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or discard, so jettisoned means dumped.

clue.text: Guarantee "Seconds out!" will lead to temper

indicators.note: out says that letter is taken away from the word for guarantee

parts.note: to insure is to guarantee against loss

explanation.surface: A boxing referee's call of seconds out leads to a show of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds out!' is the call clearing a boxing ring between rounds; here it means S is removed from INSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure is to harden or toughen by exposure, as steel is tempered, so it means temper.

clue.text: Distraught times in long story relating to knowledge

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for a long story

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem or tale

indicators.note: distraught means agitated or disturbed, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Upsetting episodes in a lengthy saga are about knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistemic is the philosophical adjective for matters of knowledge and how it is known.

clue.text: Cathedral, one rated specially to hold Mass

indicators.note: to hold says the jumbled letters take another letter inside them
specially suggests the letters are arranged in a particular new way

explanation.surface: A cathedral, rated exceptionally, holds Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass looks like a church service, fitting the cathedral, but here it is the physics term with its standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame in Paris is the famous Gothic cathedral, and many other cathedrals share the name.

clue.text: One sets off after Oxford University boat

indicators.note: after puts the word for a starter behind the university's letters

parts.note: a trigger is something that sets off a gun or a chain of events

explanation.surface: Someone launches a race following an Oxford University crew.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrigger is a racing rowing boat with projecting rowlocks, or a canoe with a float, so it is a boat.

clue.text: Clasp? Little piece broken

indicators.note: piece means only a portion of the words that come before it is used

explanation.surface: A broken fastening leaves just a fragment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' signals that the answer is a stretch of 'Clasp? Little': claSP LITtle. 'Little piece' looks like one phrase, but Little is fodder and piece the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something split has been broken apart, so split means broken.

clue.text: Contact in various routes not to be trusted

indicators.note: in places the word for contact inside the jumbled letters
various suggests the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: to reach someone is to contact them

explanation.surface: Getting in touch by assorted routes is risky business.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacherous means betraying trust or unreliable, so not to be trusted.

clue.text: Little man supporting the Spanish woman

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the man's name underneath the Spanish word

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
Len is a short form of the man's name Leonard

explanation.surface: A small man props up the Spanish woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: European politician seen in party occasion: note the strategy

indicators.note: seen in puts the politician inside the festive event

parts.note: a gala is a festive party or celebration
MEP is a Member of the European Parliament

explanation.surface: An MEP spotted at a party notes the overall approach.
explanation.definitionFit: A game plan is a planned strategy for achieving a goal.

clue.text: See 22
Sailor holding place with award for calmness

indicators.note: holding says the sailor's letters contain what follows

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A sailor with a place and a medal keeps his cool.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour limited to a small number of members.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assured composure, so it means calmness.

clue.text: Last free animal — a horse!

indicators.note: free means the letters are released from their usual order

parts.note: a lion is an animal

explanation.surface: At last an animal is free, and it is a horse!
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse.

clue.text: Lady, one from France taken in by English formally

indicators.note: taken in by puts the French word inside the letters that follow

parts.note: ice, as in icy reserve, suggests a cold formality
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman is greeted by the English with stiff formality.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'formally' piece is loose: it rests on icy formality, the cold manner of a stiff reception, which some solvers felt needed 'formality'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunice is a woman's given name, so it stands for a lady.

clue.text: Produced substance of speech

parts.note: reads as delivering the content of an address; really making vocal sounds

explanation.definitionFit: To phonate is to produce vocal sound with the voice box, the raw material of speech.
